title: Sound the horn before starting the sample conveyor
instruction: Start the conveyor: press and hold the yellow horn button so the warning sounds for at least three seconds, then press the green start button.
context: Harm: in an automated lab, a sample-tote conveyor that starts without warning catches the hand of a technician clearing a jammed tote out of the operator's sight, and can spill the samples it carries. Safe finish: horn sounded for three seconds, then the conveyor started. Rule: ASME B20.1, the conveyor safety standard, and OSHA 29 CFR 1926.555(a)(1) (an audible warning signal sounded immediately before starting a conveyor). Done by: lab automation technicians and lab staff running sample-transport lines; also conveyor operators.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is taped down; nothing is loose. Horn button: a dark plastic box 7 x 7 x 3 cm with a yellow plastic cap 4 x 4 x 1.5 cm on top that presses in 8 mm on a spring (300 N/m), at x 22, y 16, in front of the left arm. Start button: the same with a green cap, at x 22, y -16, in front of the right arm, 32 cm from the horn button. Horn lamp: a grey plastic box 5 x 5 x 3 cm on a dark plastic post 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm (5.5 cm tall in all) at x 22, y 28, beside the horn button on its outer side, 12 cm from its centre; grey, amber while the horn button is held in (on a real bench a buzzer sounds with it). Run lamp: the same lamp and post at x 22, y -28, beside the start button on its outer side; grey, green while the conveyor runs, red on a fault. Conveyor: a dark plastic block 20 cm along x, 6 cm wide and 4 cm tall, centred at x 36, y 0 (x 26 to 46), with a grey cardboard tote 5 x 5 x 4 cm standing on it at x 34; both are there to be seen, and nothing on them moves. A small controller box under the table reads both buttons and drives the lamps.
scoring: Scored at the end from the starter, which is watched every step. The horn sounds while the yellow cap is in past 70 percent of its 8 mm travel (5.6 mm); a hold is how long it stays in without a break, and any one step (0.05 s) with it out ends the hold. A start press is the green cap going in past 70 percent (it must come back under 30 percent before the next press counts). The first start press runs the conveyor (run lamp green) if the horn has been held for 3.0 s and is still held, or the latest hold of 3.0 s or more ended no more than 10.0 s before. The 10.0 s window runs from the end of that latest full hold; a shorter blast neither starts, refreshes nor cancels it. Any other first press is a fault (run lamp red) and the trial scores 0 whatever else happens: start pressed with no horn, with only blasts under 3.0 s, more than 10.0 s after the latest 3.0 s hold ended, or before any 3.0 s hold. Later presses change nothing. Conveyor running: 1.0. Horn held 3.0 s or more and start never pressed (the horn still held at the end included): 0.3. Horn held under 3.0 s, once or several times (short blasts do not add up), start never pressed: 0. Either button leaning more than 20 degrees, or its base more than 1 cm above or below its resting height (lifted, or pushed off the table), at the end: 0. Nothing done: 0. A person scores a real trial from the video, timing how long the horn lamp stays amber and the gap from it going grey to the start press, and reading the run lamp's colour, with a top photo of the two buttons at the end.
reset_notes: Let both caps spring back, check both buttons are still taped in place, and reset the controller so both lamps are grey and the horn timer is cleared. Nothing is moved or consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No horn sounds and no belt moves: the horn lamp stands for the horn and the run lamp for the conveyor, both recoloured boxes, and the conveyor and tote are fixed blocks. Nobody stands at the belt. The starter is Python watching the caps every 20 Hz step, so times count in 0.05 s steps. The buttons are spring-loaded sliders on 3 kg bodies, held by their weight rather than tape. Rubber-like friction everywhere.
